headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: xonsh can read/write and egress broadly while awesome-python is an unverified, non-runnable collection with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but xonsh can read files and run shell commands, so if awesome-python content is manually copied into xonsh, prompt-like instructions could be interpreted. awesome-python itself is a static collection with no runtime, so the pathway is indirect and unusual.
conditions: IF content from awesome-python is copied into xonsh stdin/stdout or shell scripts
IF xonsh is used to execute text taken from the collection as commands
mitigations: Keep the collection and shell session separate
Paste only vetted snippets into xonsh
Use a read-only viewer for the collection
Add a manual review step before executing copied text

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress, while awesome-python is an unverified open-source collection with no sandboxing or isolation guarantees. If both are pointed at the same workspace, xonsh can expose files or environment data to external services; the collection itself does not leak, but it can be a source of copied sensitive material.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or files
IF xonsh sends read file contents or environment variables to a remote API
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in the shared workspace
Disable outbound network access for xonsh when handling secrets
Use separate OS users or directories
Review environment variables before launching xonsh

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh has write_filesystem and execute_shell, while awesome-python is a collection that may be used as a source of scripts or configs. There is no locking or coordination primitive in either profile, so if both operate on the same directory, xonsh can overwrite or race with files referenced by the collection. The conflict is plausible in default use, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF xonsh writes files that the collection or operator also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Use file backups before xonsh writes
Serialize any file-changing steps

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python can be treated as a reference source, and xonsh can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If operator workflows copy examples from the collection into xonsh without verification, incorrect commands can cascade into real actions. The collection is not authoritative by itself, but xonsh’s execution ability makes the downstream impact meaningful.
conditions: IF examples from awesome-python are copied into xonsh and executed
IF xonsh is used to automate actions based on unreviewed snippets
mitigations: Verify commands before execution
Run examples in a disposable shell session first
Prefer documented commands over copied snippets
Require human approval for destructive commands

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source with docs-only evidence. The only compliance concern is operational: xonsh can touch environment variables and filesystem contents, so sensitive data could be handled locally if the operator places it there. The pair itself does not show a direct compliance breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files or environment variables used by xonsh
IF local handling violates an external policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the working directory
Clear sensitive environment variables before use
Use a policy-approved sandbox
Document local retention and deletion steps
